# 2 Baruch Chapter 34 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**34:1** And-it-came-to-pass after-these-things that-I-Baruch was-sitting under-an-oak, and-suddenly-a-voice came from-on-high and-said-to-me:

**34:2** Why-are-you-dismayed over-the-ruin-of-Zion? Are-you-not-learning from-everything-which-has-happened?

**34:3** For-just-as-the-rain-does-not-come-at-the-time-of-the-harvest, and-just-as-the-autumn-does-not-return-in-the-spring-[time] — so-also every-age brings-forth its-own-[portion].

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Syriac Codex Ambrosianus. Chapter 34 is a brief divine address using a seasonal analogy: each age has its proper time, just as rain does not fall at harvest. The "oak" under which Baruch sits may recall the oak at Mamre (Gen 18) or prophetic sitting places.*
